meta.name: House and garden as surveyed
meta.grid: Site grid. Origin: the outer south-east corner of the rear outshot at ground level, by the back door. +X runs south, away from the back of the house; +Y runs east, towards the road. z = 0 is level 20.00 m on the measured survey.
meta.north_note: Grid north, as a direction in (X, Y). The back of the house faces 20 degrees west of south.
meta.source: Phone clips reconstructed with COLMAP: a pan from the lawn and 60 short walks, 1,910 frames and 900,000 points in all. Vertical from brick coursing. Scale, position and height datum from eight control points read off the measured building survey (1:50 plans, 1:100 elevations). Plot boundary and north from the 1:500 block plan. Walks that leave the surveyed part and come back (round the back of the outbuilding) were reconstructed on their own and tied in through the frames they share with the rest. Ground levels from the survey points, tied to the 22 spot levels of the measured survey.
meta.accuracy: House and old shed: a few centimetres (measured survey). Outbuilding: walls within 2 cm of straight lines on all four sides, openings read off straightened photographs to 2 or 3 cm. Patio, east garden, kitchen garden, gate path, drive, front garden and the passage by the shed, all filmed on foot: 0.1 to 0.2 m. South and west garden: the east end of the south wall is now fixed to 0.1 m; the far corner still rests on the first clips, checked from a second viewpoint, and is good to about half a metre. Ground levels: a few centimetres on open ground that was filmed on foot, interpolated under shrubs and behind buildings. The lane beyond the hedge was seen only at the gate.

ground.relief_note: It has the shape of the ground: heights from the photo survey, tied to the 22 spot levels of the measured survey. The garden is nearly level round the house and the lawns, but the drive lies 0.2 to 0.27 m below the lawn, the ground rises 0.19 m against the east wall, and everything falls towards the lane: the garden gate is 0.45 m below the datum at the back door.

features.label: South wall (dark modern brick)
features.notes: Modern dark stretcher-bond brick with a red plinth, behind the big shrub and the bench. Its east end, the 3 m nearest the drive, is now fixed from a clip walked up to it: 620 survey points on its face, which put it 0.17 m nearer the house than the earlier model had it, and the whole wall has been moved by that much at this end. It stops, under ivy, about 3 m short of the brick pier on the drive: shrubs fill the gap. From the bench westwards its line still comes from the first clips (good to about 0.3 m). The top is hidden by shrubs: height 1.6 to 1.85 m.

features.label: South wall, west end (old stock brick)
features.notes: Yellow stock brick in Flemish bond with a coping: a 6 ft wall. Position and height triangulated from two clips (top of coping 1.76 m above datum, ground here about 0.08 m below it). Within about 0.3 m.

features.label: West wall (old red brick)
features.notes: Soft red brick, exposed for about 2 m behind the picnic table and ivy-covered either side. Triangulated from two clips (231 points, flat to 0.27 m). It runs about 1.2 m outside the boundary drawn on the 1:500 block plan, which is within that map's tolerance.

features.label: Ivy on the west wall
features.notes: Dense ivy standing about 2.1 m, from the exposed brick to the hazel.

features.label: Fence to the playing field
features.notes: Dark boarding glimpsed between the hazel and the outbuilding in the first clip. Its line is the wall's line carried on, and its height is a guess. Clips filmed since behind the outbuilding show no fence along its west side, only a compost bay, brambles and trees, so it is drawn no further than the corner. What marks the boundary from here north is not known.

features.label: Beech hedge along the road
features.notes: Clipped beech, 1.75 to 1.8 m tall. Its garden face is measured from a clip filmed walking along it: 9.0 m east of the grid origin beside the kitchen garden, 8.6 m further south. It starts at the garden gate, beside the big conifer; the road side is not seen along most of it, so its thickness (1.5 m) is assumed. A telegraph pole stands in it.

features.label: The house
features.notes: From the measured building survey (1:50 plans, 1:100 elevations and section): main range 8.52 x 5.66 m, rear outshot 4.38 x 4.38 m under a catslide roof that comes down to 0.9 m, ridge 7.62 m, half-hipped at both ends, three chimneys, lean-to WC on the west side. Wall positions are good to a few centimetres. The east end of the rear wing is timber-framed with brick infill, and its black frame is drawn from the east elevation and the footage. The front has an open black timber porch with a bench either side, and three first-floor oriel windows on brackets: two on the front, one at the north end of the east wall. The oriels are placed from the drawings; the porch from the survey points on its posts (1.8 m wide, standing 1.25 m out from the wall, 2.1 m high). A straightened photograph of the front made from the footage agrees with the drawn window positions to within 0.1 m. Glazing bars and joinery are indicative.

features.label: Failed render on the west gable (sheeted over)
features.notes: Condition, late November 2026: the render has come away from the west gable on both sides of the chimney stack, the larger area (about 1.7 m wide and 2.4 m high) towards the front corner, where it carries on round the corner for a metre along the front wall, up to 3 m above the ground. All of it is covered with sheeting. Cracks run up the gable above. Extent read off the straightened photograph of the front and judged by eye on the gable.

features.label: Timber shed (mossy roof)
features.notes: Footprint 2.58 x 4.41 m from the measured survey; the gable seen in the footage lands within 12 cm of it. Eaves 1.46 m and ridge 2.38 m from the footage. Vertical boards under a mossy tiled roof, with the door and a three-pane window towards the north end of the side facing the house. Condition: the frame has racked, so the long walls lean noticeably, and daylight shows between the boards. Earth floor; used for tools.

features.label: White outbuilding
features.notes: Roughcast walls under a green corrugated sheet roof that falls about 0.45 m from back to front, where a gutter runs to a downpipe at the west corner. Measured all round from clips walked along every side: the points on each wall lie within 1.5 cm of a straight line. It is not square: the front is 5.47 m long and the back 5.24, the east side 7.16 and the west 6.84, and the corner by the shed is 86.5 degrees. Worth confirming with a tape across the diagonals (the model gives 8.74 m from the front west corner to the back east corner and 8.88 m the other way). Openings are read off straightened photographs of each wall, good to 2 or 3 cm: front window 2.03 x 1.22 m and glazed door 0.87 m; east window 1.49 x 1.22 m; on the north side a door 0.82 m wide and a six-light window 1.97 m wide. The west wall has no openings in its northern 3 m; the rest of it was seen only at a glancing angle. The earlier model, from two distant clips and a view through the attic window, had the building half a metre wider and its roof falling the other way. The 1:500 block plan draws it 5.0 x 6.7 m and 1 to 2 m further east. It stands with its front threshold 0.05 m below the datum; the ground rises to 0.15 m above datum at its north-west corner.

features.label: Log store against the outbuilding
features.notes: A slatted timber store 2.0 m long, full of split logs under a pale sheet, against the north end of the east wall, below and beside the window.

features.label: Small timber shed
features.notes: A brown shiplap shed of the 6 x 4 ft kind (1.2 m wide across the gable, about 1.8 m long) under a felt roof, north-west of the outbuilding, with its door in the east gable and a small window on the south side. Logs and bags inside; the door stands open and the roof felt is torn. Its two nearer faces are placed from survey points; its length is taken from its type. It stands 2 to 3 m beyond the boundary drawn on the block plan, at the edge of the field: whose it is should be checked.

features.label: Heap under a blue tarpaulin
features.notes: Against the west wall of the outbuilding: 3.1 m long and up to 1.1 m high.

features.label: Compost bay made of pallets
features.notes: Pallets on edge beyond the tarpaulin heap, among brambles. Seen only from 6 m away at a glancing angle: position within about 0.7 m.

features.label: Wheelbarrow
features.notes: Stood on end against the north wall of the outbuilding.

features.label: Paved patio
features.notes: Old concrete flags in courses, about 0.47, 0.59 and 0.71 m (18, 24 and 28 in). The outer edge is 4.96 m long and 3.85 m from the low wall of the house. Two spot levels on the measured survey put it at 19.99 m.

features.label: Old apple tree
features.notes: Marked "Apple" on the measured survey: trunk 0.40 m across at the base, crown 4.9 m across centred 1.3 m north of the base, because the trunk leans hard towards the house. The first model had put it 0.44 m away from here using the footage alone. Height and branch pattern are indicative.

features.label: Willow (pollarded)
features.notes: Pollarded tree in front of the west wall, cut back hard: one limb sawn at about 4.4 m. Trunk about 0.6 m across. Species not confirmed. Position from the pan and one walking-clip sighting: within about a metre along the line from the middle of the lawn.

features.label: Hazel (multi-stem)
features.notes: Tall coppice in front of the ivy at the north end of the west wall; its base is hidden by the brush pile, so within about a metre.

features.label: Big old shrub with the hose
features.notes: Pale multi-stemmed shrub between the lawn and the south wall, with a coil of white hose hung in it. Stems placed from survey points.

features.label: Small twisted tree
features.notes: Stands a metre in front of the outbuilding, between its window and its door, with a heavy limb leaning out towards the shed. Trunk placed from the survey points on it.

features.label: Evergreen shrub
features.notes: At the east end of the south border.

features.label: Shrubs along the south wall
features.notes: Only just in frame. Shown as part of the border; treat as a placeholder.

features.label: Yellow-leaved coppice by the south wall
features.notes: Tall twiggy growth in front of the dark wall behind the log rounds. Species not identified.

features.label: Shrub clump in the east lawn
features.notes: An evergreen with glossy leaves and bare deciduous stems growing up through it, in a ring of bare soil: about 2 m across and 1.75 m tall. Seen from both sides.

features.label: Young tree
features.notes: A whippy young tree about 2 m tall, planted in the lawn 1.5 to 2 m in front of the hedge with perennials round its foot. Species not identified. Placed from the points on it, seen from several sides.

features.label: Young tree (pale bark)
features.notes: A staked young tree with pale bark, about 3.5 m tall and bare at the time of filming. Species not identified.

features.label: Lantern on a post
features.notes: A black lantern on a slim post beside the shrub clump, its head 1.4 m above the grass, with a pale tube on the post below it: a garden light, or a bird feeder with a baffle. Triangulated from two frames (rays meet within 2 cm).

features.label: Grey-leaved shrub
features.notes: Large silvery evergreen at the edge of the lawn; the drive is behind it.

features.label: Sage bed under the apple tree
features.notes: Overgrown bed around the pale tree: a big sage, low evergreens, twiggy stems, foxglove rosettes. Plant positions are approximate.

features.label: Sedum bed
features.notes: The bed beside the viewpoint. The pan started and ended here so only its edges were filmed; the far side of it is assumed.

features.label: Vegetable plot
features.notes: Dug over in ridges running east to west, with a few seedlings; seed trays and pots stand at its south end. Brick edgings on three sides, placed from the brick-coloured survey points and from frames with the survey grid drawn on the ground: within about 0.15 m. About 3.4 m from the path side to the hedge side and 3.6 m long.

features.label: Brick edging beside the east path
features.notes: Bricks on edge along the house side of the vegetable plot, with half a metre of grass between them and the gravel path.

features.label: Brick edging at the north end of the plot
Brick edging by the hedge
features.notes: Old red bricks laid end to end between the vegetable plot and the strip of ivy and leaf litter under the hedge: within about 0.15 m.

features.label: Brick kerb of the gate path
Brick kerb of the gate path
features.notes: The path from the corner of the house to the garden gate is a strip of old brick about 0.55 m wide between two brick kerbs, deep in leaves when filmed. It does not run square to the house: it bears a little north of east, and falls 0.35 m on the way, from 0.17 m below the datum at the house end to 0.5 m below at the gate, where it meets the pavement. The lawn on its north side dips lower still for most of its length; a grass strip separates it from the vegetable plot, which stands 0.2 m above it. Its line is taken from three things that agree: the colour of the ground in a plan made from the survey points, the track of the clip that walks it from the gate, and the view along it from the house end. Good to about 0.15 m.

Brick edging by the lawn

features.label: Boards on the ground

features.label: Cane wigwam

features.label: Folding table

features.label: Green water butt
features.notes: Stands against the south wall of the lean-to at its west corner and takes the downpipe that runs along that wall.

features.label: New fence post
features.notes: Two new sawn posts stand leaning against the west wall of the lean-to. Seen at the edge of the first clip, they were taken for gate posts across the passage: there is no gate.

features.label: Wheelie bin
features.notes: Three council bins stand in a row against the north end of the shed: two black, one with a brown lid. Placed from the survey points on them; they will move on collection days.

features.label: Old chimney pot
features.notes: A broken clay chimney pot standing against the south end of the shed, with another along the wall.

features.label: Pots along the house wall
features.notes: A dozen or so assorted pots and a trough stand along the low wall; individual pots are indicative.

features.label: Large terracotta pot
features.notes: Stands on the grass just off the west edge of the patio. Sighted from two clips.

features.label: Green glazed pot with grass
features.notes: At the south-east corner of the patio. Triangulated from three frames: the rays meet within 3 cm.

features.label: Big tree stump
features.notes: A very large stump: about 1.4 m across the cut and 0.6 m high, with root flares spreading to a little over 2 m. The earlier model, which had only seen it from across the garden, had it 1.7 m too far north. It is now fixed from close up: the glass ball that sits on it is triangulated to under a centimetre.

features.label: Glass ball
features.notes: A blue-green glass ball in the stone trough. Sighted from two frames 66 degrees apart: the rays pass within 7 mm of each other.

features.label: Green compost bin
features.notes: A small cone-shaped bin among long grass, its lid 0.76 m above datum. Triangulated from two frames (rays meet within a centimetre). The earlier model had it 1.1 m away.

features.label: Blue ride-on toy
features.notes: Lying on the lawn in the later clips, where the first clips showed something blue that was taken for a tarp. It will have moved since.

features.label: Pop-up goal
features.notes: By the hedge, its mouth towards the lawn. The top of the arch is triangulated; which way it faces is judged from how narrow it looks from the north.

features.label: Garden gate
features.notes: A white picket gate between two square posts, 1.05 m apart, opening straight onto the pavement. The ground here is 0.45 m below the datum at the house. It leans, and was filmed both shut and open. Placed from the survey points on its posts.

features.label: Big conifer by the gate
features.notes: A dark evergreen with a bare red-brown trunk for its first 2 m, standing in the hedge line on the south side of the gate and overhanging the vegetable plot. Position within about half a metre; height 9 to 10 m by eye.

features.label: Yellow-leaved shrub
features.notes: A bright mass of yellow leaves 2.5 m across on the north side of the gate, where a hedge would be.

features.label: Wishing well
features.notes: An ornamental well in the front lawn: a brick drum 0.95 m across, two posts with a windlass and a little tiled roof, its ridge running north to south. Triangulated from two frames; within about 0.15 m.

features.label: Leaning tree in the front garden
features.notes: A mossy-trunked tree, still in yellow leaf, leaning hard towards the north-east corner over the tarpaulin. Species not identified. Trunk placed from 190 survey points; height and branches are indicative.

features.label: Heap under a blue tarpaulin
features.notes: About 3 x 2.4 m, under the leaning tree in the north-east corner. What is under it is not known.

features.label: Old roof tiles on the ground
features.notes: Clay plain tiles and a ridge tile or two spread over about 2 x 2 m of ground and half grown over with ivy. Worth counting: they match the roof.

Evergreen bush in the front lawn
Shrub in front of the right-hand window
features.notes: A thin shrub with pale stems, a rose by the look of it, at the edge of the gravel.

features.label: Black pot by the front wall
Cut branches stacked by the north boundary
Overgrown north boundary
features.notes: A belt of shrubs, brambles and young trees 2 to 4 m deep along the whole north side: the lawn stops at its edge, about 7.5 m from the front of the house. Whatever marks the boundary itself (a fence or an old hedge) is hidden inside it. The inner edge is measured; its depth is taken from the block plan.

features.label: Shrubs in the north-east corner
features.notes: Between the yellow shrub and the corner there is no clipped hedge, only shrubs and brambles with the road behind them.

features.label: Brick kerb between the lawn and the drive
features.notes: Bricks laid flat in a curve where the lawn meets the gravel. The gravel is the lower side: the drive lies 0.2 to 0.27 m below the lawn here.

features.label: Timber sleeper edging
features.notes: A sleeper holding back the shrub bed along the west side of the drive, 2.4 m long, carrying on the line of the brick kerb.

features.label: Paved strip across the drive entrance
features.notes: A line of block pavers set flush in the gravel, from the end of the low wall to the brick pier: it marks where this drive stops and the gravel shared with the neighbour begins. Cars reach the road across that gravel, so there is no gate or opening of this plot's own onto the road. Triangulated at both ends and the middle. It runs 0.5 to 0.8 m outside the boundary drawn on the 1:500 block plan, and parallel to it.

features.label: Brick pier at the end of the south wall
features.notes: Red brick, 0.44 m square and 1.0 m high (13 courses), where the paved strip ends. 125 survey points on it.

features.label: Low brick wall beside the drive
features.notes: Red brick, about 1.2 m high from the gravel, running from the road hedge to the drive entrance. Position from 330 survey points on its face. A boarded fence and a copper beech hedge stand behind it on the neighbour's side; which of them owns the wall is not known.

features.label: Neighbour's fence behind the low wall
features.notes: Seen over the wall with a beech hedge growing through it. Height estimated.

features.label: Road hedge, cut back hard
features.notes: Beside the drive the beech hedge has been cut back to bare stems and brushwood about 1.5 m high, held with a stake. Its line is carried on from the measured hedge; the road side is not seen.

features.label: Bulk bag of garden waste

features.label: Neighbour's garage
features.notes: Brick, with a brown up-and-over door facing the shared gravel. Its nearest corner is fixed by survey points (16.7, -4.85): the 1:500 block plan draws that corner 2 m further east. Its depth and height are judged by eye. Massing only.

features.label: Neighbour's house (west)

features.label: Telegraph pole

features.notes: About 1,035 square metres. Map accuracy is about a metre: the west wall measured from the footage runs 1.2 m outside this line, the south wall sits on it.

features.label: Outbuilding as drawn on the block plan
features.notes: 5.0 x 6.7 m on the map. The footage agrees with its depth and its north end, but puts the building 1 to 2 m further west and makes it 6.0 m wide. Tree cover over the west end may be why the map draws it short.

features.label: Grid origin
features.notes: Outer south-east corner of the rear outshot at ground level. X runs south from here, Y runs east. To do 6: a few tape or laser measurements would check the model where it matters. The outer edge of the patio (the model says 4.96 m); the apple tree trunk to the exposed brick of the west wall (15.2 m); the south-west corner of the outshot to the west front corner of the outbuilding (14.3 m); the outbuilding front (5.47 m) and its two diagonals (8.74 and 8.88 m); the north-east corner of the house to the nearer gate post (8.4 m). The full list is in SURVEY_TODO.md.

features.label: Drain between the chambers (assumed line)
features.notes: The inverts fall 0.14 m from IC2 to IC1, so the flow is towards the lawn. The route is drawn straight between the covers; where it goes from IC1 is not known.

features.label: To film 1: South and west walls again, from further back
features.notes: Three clips filmed close against the brickwork could not be joined to the survey: a wall of bricks looks the same everywhere, and the software lost its bearings. Walk the same line 3 to 4 m out from the walls with the camera pointing along the garden, so that every frame has the wall on one side and the lawn, the trees and the buildings in the rest. Start and finish on the patio. Until then the far corner still rests on the first clips (about half a metre).

features.label: To film 5: Roof and chimneys
features.notes: Still photos rather than video: each roof slope and each chimney, zoomed in, from the far corners of the garden and from the road.

features.label: To film 7: Inside the outbuilding: the partition
features.notes: The clips filmed inside did not show the wall between the two rooms squarely, so where it stands is still a judgement (3.5 m back from the front, give or take 0.3 m). Either tape each room, or stand in the middle of each and turn slowly through a full circle with the lights on.

features.label: To film 8: Inside the shed
features.notes: The clips taken inside were too dark to join up. Open the door wide, stand in the doorway and film each end from floor to roof; then step back out with the camera running.

features.label: To film 9: Inside the house: rooms not yet filmed
features.notes: All three storeys are in the model from the floor plans: open the house with the Attic, First floor and Ground floor buttons. Each room card says whether it has been filmed. For the rest, one clip per room: stand in a corner and turn slowly for 20 to 30 seconds, lights on, curtains open.

features.label: To film 10: West side of the outbuilding and the field edge
features.notes: The west wall was only seen at a glancing angle past the tarpaulin heap, and the small shed only from two sides. Walk from the north-west corner of the outbuilding down its west side to the lawn, then film the small shed from the field side. What marks the boundary here (the fence line, and whether the small shed is inside it) has not been seen.

features.label: To film 11: North boundary
features.notes: A belt of shrubs 2 to 4 m deep hides whatever marks the boundary on the north side. If you can get in at any point, film the fence or hedge inside it; otherwise a tape from the front wall of the house to the fence at two places would do.
